chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from 'Ali ibn al-Nu'man, from Abi al-Sabbah al-Kinani, from Abi 'Abdillah عليه السلام, who said:

Regarding a man who dies while traveling in a land where none are with him except women, he said: he is to be buried and not given ghusl (ritual washing). And a woman who is with men in that same situation is buried and not given ghusl (ritual washing).

key_terms.الرِّجَالِ: men present with the deceased woman
key_terms.السَّفَرِ: travel; the circumstance in which this ruling applies
key_terms.النِّسَاءُ: women present with the deceased man
key_terms.الْمَرْأَةُ: the female deceased in the parallel ruling
key_terms.يُغَسَّلُ: he or she is given ghusl (ritual washing of the deceased)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a man or woman dies during travel and only unrelated members of the opposite sex are present?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling for cases of death during travel when only unrelated members of the opposite sex are present. It states that in such circumstances the deceased is to be buried without ghusl (ritual washing), reflecting the limits of bodily handling between non-mahrams.
